# Data handling

#### Loading data and creating subset

```{r Dota load and subsetting}
# Load the children dataset from a .SAV file 

#depending on computer C:/Users/Rik/OneDrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/1_Study_1_Physical_access/Data/DATA/Uganda Full/DHS Clusters/UGKR7BSV_Children/UGKR7BFL.SAV   

DHS_children_sub <- read_sav("D:/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/1_Study_1_Physical_access/Data/DATA/Uganda Full/DHS Clusters/UGKR7BSV_Children/UGKR7BFL.SAV")


# Filter out rows with children who are no longer alive (B5 == 1)
DHS_children_sub = subset(DHS_children_sub, B5 == 1)

# Keep only children with anthropometric measurements (non-missing HW5 values)
DHS_children_sub = DHS_children_sub %>% drop_na(HW5)

Kamp = subset(DHS_children_sub, V024 == 0)

DHS_loc <- st_read("D:/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/1_Study_1_Physical_access/Data/DATA/Uganda Full/DHS Clusters/UGGE7AFL/UGGE7AFL.shp")

# Only select 
DHS_loc <- subset(DHS_loc, ADM1NAME == "KAMPALA")


Kamp <- Kamp %>%
  group_by(V001) %>%
  summarise(Count = n()) %>%
  mutate(V001 = reorder(V001, Count)) # Reorder V001 based on Count

# Rename V001 to DHSCUST
names(Kamp)[names(Kamp) == "V001"] <- "DHSCLUST"

DHS_loc <- merge(DHS_loc, Kamp, by = "DHSCLUST", all.x = TRUE)

# Read the shapefile
parishes <- st_read("D:/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/2_Study_2_Flooding_Analysis/Data/Processed/Adm_boundaries_parishes/Parishes_Kamp_UTM36N.shp")

# Reproject the parishes shapefile to the same projection as the DHS location data
parishes <- st_transform(parishes, st_crs(DHS_loc))

map = ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = parishes, fill = "lightgray", color = "black") +  # Add the shapefile as a base layer
  geom_point(data = DHS_loc, aes(x = LONGNUM, y = LATNUM, size = Count, color = Count), alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Children per Cluster in Kampala", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 10), name = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right")

# Summary statistics of the count variable
summary(Kamp$Count)

# Create a bar plot of the cluster distribution
ggplot(Kamp, aes(x = DHSCLUST, y = Count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") + # Use 'identity' to use Count values directly
  labs(title = "Distribution of Clusters in Kampala", x = "Cluster", y = "Count") +
  theme_bw() + # Use a black and white theme
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"), # Increase title size and make it bold
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12), # Increase axis label size
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10), # Increase axis tick label size
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    panel.border = element_blank(), # Remove plot border
    legend.position = "none") + # Remove legend
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(Kamp$Count), by = 1)) + # Add more y ticks
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq(0, max(Kamp$Count), by = 1), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray") # Add dotted lines

```

## Rainfall data
### Daily rainfall data
```{r}

df <- data.frame(
  Combination = c("40mm_1hr", "40mm_2hr", "40mm_3hr", "80mm_1hr", "80mm_2hr", "80mm_3hr", "120mm_1hr", "120mm_2hr", "120mm_3hr"),
  Rainfall = c(40, 40, 40, 80, 80, 80, 120, 120, 120),
  Duration = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3),
  Healthcare_Coverage = c(90, 75, 60, 75, 60, 45, 60, 45, 30)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x = Combination, y = Healthcare_Coverage, fill = factor(Rainfall))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_line(aes(group = Rainfall), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), linewidth = 3) +
  labs(title = "Healthcare Coverage by Rainfall and Duration", x = "Combination", y = "Healthcare Coverage") +
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "Rainfall (mm)", labels = c("40mm", "80mm", "120mm")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top") + 
      scale_x_discrete(limits = c("40mm_1hr", "40mm_2hr", "40mm_3hr", "80mm_1hr", "80mm_2hr", "80mm_3hr", "120mm_1hr", "120mm_2hr", "120mm_3hr"))


ggplot(df, aes(x = Combination, y = Healthcare_Coverage, fill = factor(Duration))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_line(aes(group = Duration), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), linewidth = 3) +
  labs(title = "Healthcare Coverage by Rainfall and Duration", x = "Combination", y = "Healthcare Coverage") +
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "Duration (hours)", labels = c("1 hour", "2 hours", "3 hours")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top") +
      scale_x_discrete(limits = c("40mm_1hr", "40mm_2hr", "40mm_3hr", "80mm_1hr", "80mm_2hr", "80mm_3hr", "120mm_1hr", "120mm_2hr", "120mm_3hr"))

      # Line plot of Healthcare Coverage by Rainfall and Duration
      ggplot(df, aes(x = Combination, y = Healthcare_Coverage, group = Rainfall, color = factor(Rainfall))) +
        geom_line() +
        labs(title = "Healthcare Coverage by Rainfall and Duration", x = "Combination", y = "Healthcare Coverage") +
        scale_color_discrete(name = "Rainfall (mm)", labels = c("40mm", "80mm", "120mm")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
              axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
              panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
              panel.border = element_blank()) +
              scale_x_discrete(limits = c("40mm_1hr", "40mm_2hr", "40mm_3hr", "80mm_1hr", "80mm_2hr", "80mm_3hr", "120mm_1hr", "120mm_2hr", "120mm_3hr"))
```

# Flood scenarios
```{r}
# Load all .img files in the specified folder
file_path <- "D:/AM5_flood_project/out/2024-03-19-16-03-54/All"
file_list <- list.files(file_path, pattern = "\\.img$", full.names = TRUE)

# Load all rasters 
raster_list <- lapply(file_list, rast)

# Label the raster files with the corresponding file names
names(raster_list) <- file_list

# load all rasters as seperate objects
MLC100_10800 = raster_list[[1]]
MLC100_21600 = raster_list[[2]]
MLC100_3600 = raster_list[[3]]

MLC20_10800 = raster_list[[4]]
MLC20_21600 = raster_list[[5]]
MLC20_3600 = raster_list[[6]]

MLC40_10800 = raster_list[[7]]
MLC40_21600 = raster_list[[8]]
MLC40_3600 = raster_list[[9]]

MLC60_10800 = raster_list[[10]]
MLC60_21600 = raster_list[[11]]
MLC60_3600 = raster_list[[12]]

MLC80_10800 = raster_list[[13]]
MLC80_21600 = raster_list[[14]]
MLC80_3600 = raster_list[[15]]

x = c(MLC20_3600, MLC20_10800, MLC20_21600, MLC40_3600, MLC40_10800, MLC40_21600, MLC60_3600, MLC60_10800, MLC60_21600, MLC80_3600, MLC80_10800, MLC80_21600, MLC100_3600, MLC100_10800, MLC100_21600)

names(x) <- c("MLC20_3600", "MLC20_10800", "MLC20_21600", "MLC40_3600", "MLC40_10800", "MLC40_21600", "MLC60_3600", "MLC60_10800", "MLC60_21600", "MLC80_3600", "MLC80_10800", "MLC80_21600", "MLC100_3600", "MLC100_10800", "MLC100_21600")

# Create a grid of the plots
gridplot = panel(x, col = data.frame(from = c(0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180), 
              to = c(15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, Inf), 
              color = colorRampPalette(c("light green", "red"))(8)),
              nr = 5, nc = 3,
              axes = FALSE
)

# save the gridplot as a pdf
png("D:/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/2_Study_2_Flooding_Analysis/Plots/flood_scenarios.png", width = 20, height = 30, units = "cm", res = 600)
print(gridplot)
dev.off()
```
